recorded_from: the Next.js handler at 03149a4, by scripts/contracts/record-repo-starred.mjs
boundary: The Supabase cookie-session client and GitHub are replaced; the real handler runs. GitHub requests are listed sorted by URL, since up to four run at once.

cases.reason: No session: 401, and neither the database nor GitHub is asked.
If the Supabase client cannot be built: 500 with a fixed sentence.
A database error: 500 with a fixed sentence, and GitHub is not asked.
No rows: an empty list, marked private and not stored.
Every row is checked again with GitHub. Six public fields replace the stored snapshot, which is never trusted; the other columns and the notes are kept as they are.
A repository GitHub says is private, or one whose privacy is not an explicit false, gets null: a visitor never sees private metadata.
Not found, a server error, a refused redirect, no connection and a reply that is not JSON all give null for that row only.
A field GitHub leaves out is left out of repo_data too; a field that is null stays null.
A stored name must be exactly owner/name with safe characters, or GitHub is not asked and repo_data is null.
Rows keep the database order (newest first) and every row is asked about, the same repository twice included.
Nine rows: all nine are asked about (at most four at a time; the Node runner checks that separately) and keep their order.
An anonymous Supabase account is a user, so its own rows are returned.
Stored columns and GitHub values pass through unchanged: text outside ASCII, very large numbers, nested objects.
